approval.note: A composed script is a draft. A human reads it before this film is published anywhere.

script.vo01: Product owners write requirements and acceptance criteria from a blank page, and the quality depends on who is writing that day. Templates exist but are rarely reused, so the same structure gets rebuilt each time.
script.vo02: Innovation submissions arrive uneven, and a good idea inside a thin write-up is easy to miss.
script.vo03: It reads Requirements and acceptance criteria templates, Existing backlog items. It engages you in Microsoft 365 Copilot and Teams. And it can draft requirements and acceptance criteria from the approved template, showing the reasoning behind every answer.
script.vo04: A product owner describes a feature idea. The agent returns requirements and acceptance criteria in the approved structure, reusing patterns already in the backlog rather than inventing new ones.
script.vo05: Asked what still needs a decision, the agent separates what it could derive from the idea from the choices only the business can make, and frames each of those as a question.
script.vo06: On risk, the agent shows where the acceptance criteria are untestable as written, proposes a measurable form for each, and flags the assumption behind the rest.
script.vo_payoff: Product owners start from a structured draft, and requirement quality stops depending on who wrote it.
script.vo_helps: The result? A quicker first draft, requirement quality that holds across authors, and a guided page in place of a blank one.
script.vo_cta: Get started on your agentic journey today. Talk to your Microsoft representative to learn more.
